name: Jadwa Investment
legal_name: Jadwa Investment Company (Saudi closed joint stock company)
founded: 2006 (incorporated 21 Aug 2006 and licensed by the CMA the same day; business commenced 19 Feb 2007)
ownership_summary: Unlisted Saudi closed joint stock company with SAR 1.0bn paid-up capital (100,000,000 shares of SAR 10). The FY2025 annual report states that after a 2022 buy-back of 10% of its shares from 'the sole foreign investor' the company is 100% owned by Saudi shareholders; those treasury shares (SAR 170.5m at 31 Dec 2025) were allocated to the employee share plan. The individual shareholders and their percentages are not disclosed in the sources opened (checked 2026-10-12).
government_link: No government shareholding disclosed in company materials (checked 2026-10-12): the FY2025 annual report says only that the firm is owned by Saudi shareholders. Government-related entities are among its clients (S1 p.6, S2).
group_structure: Jadwa Investment Company (Riyadh) is the operating parent and holds the CMA licence. Wholly owned subsidiaries: Jadwa Investment (DIFC) Limited (DFSA-licensed), and four Cayman Islands entities used for international advisory and fund structures. It manages the listed Jadwa REIT Saudi Fund and Jadwa REIT Al Haramain Fund (both on the Saudi Exchange). Board (S4, S1 p.7): Adib Alzamil (Chairman), Abdulaziz Alsubeaei (Vice Chairman), Abdulrahman Al-Ruwaita, Chris Masterson (independent), Khalid Al-Khowaiter (independent), Iqbal Khan (independent), Michael Powell (independent; chairs the Investment Committee), Dr Sadek Wahba (independent), Tariq Al-Sudairy (Managing Director & CEO). Shariah Board (S5): Dr Abdullah Al-Mutlaq (Chairman), Dr Mohamed Elgari, Bader Al-Omar, Dr Ahmed Al-Gaidy. The Executive Management Committee also includes the Chief Economist (Toby Iles), the General Legal Counsel and Corporate Secretary (Naif Abuhaimed) and the Head of Human Resources (Naif Al-Mutairi) (S3). Board committees: Audit and Risk, Compliance, Investment, Remuneration and Compensation (S1 p.33).

subsidiaries.name: Jadwa Investment (DIFC) Limited
subsidiaries.activity: DFSA-licensed: advising on financial products, arranging credit and advising on credit, arranging deals in investments, managing assets (Dubai)

subsidiaries.name: Jadwa Investment Management Company
subsidiaries.activity: Advisory services to international funds managed by Jadwa (Cayman Islands)

subsidiaries.name: Jadwa International PE Fund GP Limited
subsidiaries.activity: General partner entity, international private equity fund (Cayman Islands)

footprint: Headquartered in Riyadh (moved to a new head office at Laysen Valley, Tower 8, in 2025) with 'three regional offices' (S1, S2). The offices are not named on the official pages opened; a LinkedIn company snippet seen in search results lists Jeddah, Al-Khobar and Dubai (S22). DFSA-licensed subsidiary in Dubai (DIFC). Brokerage reaches Tadawul, ADX, DFM, NASDAQ Dubai, Bahrain Bourse, Boursa Kuwait, Muscat Stock Exchange and Qatar Stock Exchange (S9). Signed a State Street MoU for Oman on 1 Jun 2026 (S18).
customer_segments: Government-related entities, local and international institutional investors, family offices, non-profit endowments, corporates and 'private wealth investors' (FY2025 annual report). Multi-asset funds and some products are restricted to qualified investors (S11). No published minimums or wealth tiers.
business_lines: Public markets (Saudi, GCC, MENA, developed and emerging equity; sukuk and fixed income; money market; segregated mandates/DPMs); private equity (GCC Diversified PE Fund, GCC Private Equity Fund I, international PE co-investment funds, mezzanine); real estate (private development and income funds, plus listed REITs Jadwa REIT Saudi and Jadwa REIT Al Haramain); private credit (GCC Diversified Private Credit Fund, mezzanine commodity-murabaha funds, international structured credit); multi-asset funds and a multi-asset discretionary account and fund platform; investment advisory (non-discretionary and discretionary/fiduciary, multi-manager funds for institutions and family offices); dealing/brokerage; investment banking advisory (IPO, M&A, privatisation - stated as not a main activity); economic research. All offerings are Shariah-compliant.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Jadwa is a CMA-licensed, wholly Shariah-compliant manufacturer of investment products. At 31 Dec 2025 it had SAR 100.99bn of AUM plus SAR 17.26bn under advisement (SAR 118.24bn in total). Clients are mainly government entities, institutions, family offices and endowments, with 'private wealth investors' served by a Private and Institutional Client Investments unit that uses relationship managers, a client service call centre (added 2025), a web portal and a mobile app. The shelf is its own: public equity, sukuk and money-market funds, segregated mandates, multi-asset funds (2023) with a multi-asset discretionary account and fund platform, private equity, real estate and private credit blind-pool funds, and multi-manager funds that use third-party managers. The 2025 annual report states a goal of broadening client reach through partnerships with commercial banks and fintech platforms, without naming them.

private_banking.detail: Not a bank. A Private and Institutional Client Investments unit (head: Ghannam Al-Ghannam) handles client relationship development and servicing across all offices; clients include private wealth investors, dedicated relationship managers and, since 2025, a dedicated client service call centre and an upgraded coverage model. No wealth tiers or minimums published.

asset_management.detail: Core business. AUM SAR 100.99bn at 31 Dec 2025 (public markets AUM SAR 66.2bn). Moody's reaffirmed its MQ1 investment-manager quality rating (highest on its scale) per the annual report. In 2025 all Saudi and GCC public equity strategies outperformed their benchmarks by 1.87 to 11.76 percentage points; Asset Manager of the Year at the Saudi Tadawul Group forum (company claim). Real estate AUM about SAR 26bn (Jul 2026, news). Private equity invested capital SAR 10.7bn and real estate invested capital SAR 34.2bn cumulative (company figures, annual report p.9).

brokerage.detail: Jadwa is CMA-licensed for dealing and offers brokerage across Tadawul, ADX, DFM, NASDAQ Dubai, Bahrain Bourse, Boursa Kuwait, Muscat and Qatar exchanges via phone, web portal and mobile app, plus IPO and rights-issue subscription on Tadawul. Direct online trading is described for Tadawul. In 2025 it executed over 302,465 orders and negotiated deals above SAR 4.98bn, mainly for its investment management clients. Core trading system and omnibus account were upgraded in 2025 (vendor not named). Overseen by the COO.

digital_investing.detail: Corporate website, online account opening, web portal, mobile app, online subscription platform and online KYC update were unveiled over 2022-2024; 2025 added online registration, open banking capabilities, instant IBAN verification, real-time deposits and real-time online FX rates and transfers. The app lets clients view investments, download statements, subscribe to and redeem funds, transfer money and trade on Tadawul in real time (Argaam, Jun 2024). Relationship managers remain the main service model. No app-user numbers published; platform vendor not named.

advisory.detail: Investment advisory practice for institutions, endowments, family offices and corporates: strategic asset allocation, investment policy, manager selection, operational set-up and monitoring; both non-discretionary and discretionary advisory. Advisory mandates SAR 17.26bn and fiduciary mandates SAR 10.14bn at Dec 2025; SAR 9.87bn of new and expanded mandates won in 2025. Best Performing Endowment Fund award from the General Authority of Awqaf (company claim). Also advisory on investment banking (IPO, M&A, privatisation) but 'not among the firm's main activities'.

discretionary.detail: Segregated mandates (DPMs) in sukuk/fixed income and public equity; a Shariah-compliant fiduciary platform with access to external fund managers; and a multi-asset discretionary account and fund platform offering tailored asset allocation, priority allocation to Jadwa funds and reduced investment minimums (annual report). Fiduciary management mandates SAR 10.14bn at Dec 2025.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or digital model-portfolio service found. Equivalent risk-profile products exist as fund wrappers: Global and Saudi Concentrated Conservative, Balanced and Growth multi-asset funds (launched 2023; Balanced/Growth restricted to qualified investors), plus the multi-asset discretionary account and fund platform.

funds_platform.detail: Multi-manager and multi-asset funds that invest through external managers across liquid and illiquid assets (portfolio SAR 12.57bn at Dec 2025): e.g. Developed Markets Passive Equity (2020), Emerging Markets Quantitative Equity (2020), International Sukuk Fund (2020), Multi-Manager International Private Equity Fund (2021), International Structured Credit Fund (2020). These are Jadwa-branded wrappers over third-party managers. No open third-party funds shelf or platform provider found. A 2015 Allfunds distribution agreement exists for offshore distribution of Jadwa funds (historical).

structured_products.detail: No structured notes or capital-protected products found in the annual report or product pages. 'Structured corporate credit' (Jadwa International Structured Credit Fund) is a private credit fund, not a structured product.

private_markets.detail: Private equity: Jadwa GCC Diversified Private Equity Fund (first regional blind-pool, SAR 1.3bn after second close in 2025; third close expected H1 2026), Jadwa GCC Private Equity Fund I, international PE co-investment funds (Co-investment Fund 3 now 9% deployed in 14 investments). Real estate: 26 funds active in 2025, two new local funds (SAR 960m), up to SAR 10bn of Makkah development funds announced Jul 2026. Private credit: Jadwa GCC Diversified Private Credit Fund (target up to SAR 750m, first close over SAR 300m, announced 14 Jan 2026; offered to institutional and private wealth investors), mezzanine murabaha funds, international structured credit and real-asset debt funds. 13 PE and private credit blind-pool funds launched to date.

islamic_wealth.detail: Whole firm is Shariah-compliant. Shariah Board: Dr Abdullah Al-Mutlaq (Chairman), Dr Mohamed Elgari, Bader Al-Omar, Dr Ahmed Al-Gaidy; in-house Shariah compliance team ran 110 research studies in 2025. Euromoney named it Middle East's best Islamic fund manager 2026 (company and press claim). Sukuk funds, murabaha/liquidity funds, Shariah-compliant REITs.

opportunities: States a strategy of expanding partnerships with commercial banks and fintech platforms to broaden client reach, with no partners named (FY2025 annual report, S1 p.21).

Wants private wealth clients to diversify through blind-pool PE and private credit funds and says multi-asset offerings carry reduced minimums; 13 blind-pool funds launched, including the Jan 2026 private credit fund aimed at private wealth investors (S1, S13).

Uses third-party GPs and managers for international exposure (multi-manager and co-investment funds, SAR 12.57bn at Dec 2025), which shows an existing sourcing model for outside alternatives and funds (S10, S1).
No robo-advisor, model-portfolio app or structured-products offering found; digital channel is a client portal and app for its own funds and Tadawul trading (S1, S9, S15).
Growth intent in real estate (SAR 26bn to SAR 50bn target) and private credit points to a larger own-product shelf that needs distribution (S16, S13).
barriers: Shariah-only manufacturer: any partner product would need Shariah Board approval, and the firm's own funds dominate the shelf (S5, S1, S6).
Built and iterated its own digital stack (web portal, app, online account opening, KYC, subscription platform) in 2022-2025 and upgraded its core trading system in 2025 (S1).
Relationship-manager led, institution-weighted client base; no published wealth tiers, client numbers or retail digital onboarding metrics (S1, S3).
Not a bank: no deposits, and securities custody is licensed but not a main activity, so it may rely on third parties for custody and asset servicing (S1 p.33, S18).

discrepancies.detail: Official pages show different undated totals: homepage 118.2bn 'client assets' (S8); overview AUM 100.9bn + advisement 17.3bn (S2); 'Our firm' page SAR 102.7bn 'under management and advisement' (S7); annual report 'more than 115 billion' on the profile page but 118.24bn in the statements and business overview (S1 p.6 vs p.17, p.22); press release 'more than SAR 110bn' (S13).
discrepancies.resolution: Used the annual report: AUM 100.99bn, advisement 17.26bn, total 118.24bn at 31 Dec 2025. The 102.7bn on the 'Our firm' page looks like an older year-end figure but is unverified.

discrepancies.detail: Statements show net income after zakat SAR 262,717,529; the CEO statement and highlights say 261.62m, which equals total comprehensive income after a SAR 1.1m remeasurement loss.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded SAR 262,717,529 as net_profit from the income statement.

discrepancies.detail: Narrative 'total revenues of 762.17 million' vs statement 'Total operating income' SAR 761,057,154 (762.17m is probably operating income plus other income, 0.67m + 0.44m, plus rounding; not reconciled).
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded the statement line as operating_income.

discrepancies.detail: Jadwa bio says Tariq Al-Sudairy joined in 2011; Forbes Middle East says he has led Jadwa since 2014.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded 2014 as the CEO start with the note; no conflict on the current role.

discrepancies.detail: A third-party search summary listed 'Abdullah Al Eisa' as Head of Treasury in a 2025 aggregator profile, while Jadwa's page lists him as COO.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the official page (COO); the aggregator was not opened or cited.

open_items: Shareholders and percentages not disclosed: the annual report says 100% Saudi-owned after a 2022 buy-back of 10% from 'the sole foreign investor' (not named). Search results mention a 2008 Khazanah Nasional announcement of a 10% stake; the link to the 2022 buy-back is unconfirmed. Check the Ministry of Commerce register or CMA filings.

CMA register not checked: cma.gov.sa returned 'The requested URL was rejected' (bot protection, not bypassed). Licence 06034-37 and activities are from Jadwa's own corporate information page (S6) and the annual report. DFSA public register for Jadwa Investment (DIFC) Limited not checked.
Business Wire copy of the 14 Jan 2026 release returned 403; the jadwa.com copy was used (S13).

No 30 Jun 2026 or 30 Sep 2026 financial statements for Jadwa Investment Company found; the FY2025 audited statements are the latest. Auditor name not extracted. The Pillar III 2025 disclosure PDF (https://www.jadwa.com/sites/default/files/2026-03/Jadwa_Pillar-3%202025%20En%20for%20website.pdf) was downloaded but not used for metrics.

No technology or wealth-platform vendor named anywhere (app, web portal, core trading system, omnibus account). No Head of Digital identified; the 2024 org chart (S21) shows none and the COO oversees IT and brokerage.

A LinkedIn search result titled 'Jad Desphy - CEO - Jadwa Investment' appeared repeatedly. It was not corroborated by any official or news source, which name Tariq Al-Sudairy as Managing Director & CEO; probably an unrelated or stale profile. Not recorded as a person.

LinkedIn not verified for Abdullah Al-Eisa, Abdullah Al Zouman and Fidaa Haddad; not checked for Alzamil, Alsubeaei, Afiouni, Hussain and Al-Omar. Abdullah Al Kharsan's title (Head of Brokerage and Administration) rests on a search snippet only.
Abdullah Al Zouman (MD, Multi-Asset Solutions) and Fidaa Haddad (MD, Head of Private Credit) are not on the official Management Team page; Haddad is confirmed by Jadwa's own Jan 2026 release.

Named distribution partners (banks, fintechs) behind the 'partnerships with commercial banks and fintech platforms' statement were not found; the 2015 Allfunds agreement has no current-status evidence. Argaam interview (Jun 2024) mentions in-person service by relationship managers; no app-user figures.
Real estate AUM of about SAR 26bn rests on Arab News (6 Jul 2026), with no stated as-of date; the Jadwa LinkedIn post and Asharq Bloomberg interview behind it were not opened.
Jadwa has not published a regulated fund-distribution or retail-platform channel list; whether public funds are sold through third-party banks was not found.
